column1: # bench/bounded ACROSS A SET VERSION AND A PIN -- a READ of pinned records, not a measurement.
# rule         : the two sets NEVER POOL (bench/bounded/NOTES.md). Only cells whose pattern id AND subject id
#                exist in both -- with EQUAL pattern canonical_sha256 and EQUAL subject sha256/bytes -- are
#                emitted, one row per (pattern, subject, regime, form, testee config). Cell against cell, never sum against sum.
# comparable   : pcrecbench.reduce.reduce_match_cell -- median over trials of per-row elapsed_ns/iterations;
#                ratio = after / before, so > 1 is SLOWER at the newer pin. A cell with any failing or gave-up
#                trial on either side carries its outcome in `note` and NO ratio.
# forms        : match-compliance is measured on the WHOLE-SUBJECT artifact, every other regime on `plain`
#                (adapters.py:form_for_regime); the two are different machines and never share a row.
# CAVEAT       : `iterations` is calibrated per (pattern, regime) over the WHOLE subject set of that regime
#                (harness.calibrate), and 0.3 changed both pools -- it appends match-only subjects up to 1024 B
#                and moves `short_search_max_bytes` 512 -> 258. So the two sides of a row may be timed at
#                DIFFERENT iteration counts even where the work is byte-identical: the `before_iters` /
#                `after_iters` columns carry them, and a ratio whose two sides differ by a large factor there is
#                a candidate calibration effect, not a pin effect. This file states the fact; it does not rule.
# patterns     : 30 in BEFORE, 43 in AFTER, 30 ids in common, 30 byte-identical (the emitted surface)
# subjects     : 35 in BEFORE, 54 in AFTER, 35 ids in common, 35 byte-identical (the emitted surface)
# REJECTED     : none -- every shared id is byte-identical on both sides (0.3's own no-drift promise, checked here)
